brightData: Pipeline (/workspace/benny/pipeline/pipeline.py) supports --fetcher brightdata (Web Unlocker, BRIGHTDATA_API_TOKEN saved), but the v2026-10-24 snapshot fetched 19/20 cards with the plain fetcher. Bright Data only retrieves pages; the extractor decides what is captured. Current extractor keeps perks only when they need enrollment (22 perks, all requiresActivation), so non-enrollment perks (lounges, Global Entry/TSA credit, DashPass, status) are missing.
caveatRules: Derived deterministically from each rule's verbatim quote + fields: Enroll first; Only after you pay for X (auto-renewing/membership/subscription); Spend $N first; Book through issuer travel site (earn rules only when label is travel); Up to cap, then base rate; Only <condition>; Excludes ...; U.S. only; Only at merchants; Resets monthly/no carryover; Subject to availability; protections: terms not confirmed / secondary / decline rental CDW. Tips: worth it only if you'd pay anyway; conditional rate not counted; annual fee vs annualized credits; points no fixed cash value.
nextIdeas: Widen extractor schema: perk.kind (lounge|status|membership|travel_credit|insurance|other), perk.requires {enrollment, paidMembership, minSpend{amount,windowDays}, bookingChannel, authorizedUserFee}, valueUsd when stated; rerun with --fetcher brightdata for JS/blocked issuer pages + benefit guides (PDF).
Spend-gated perks: progress bar from purchases (e.g. $X of $Y toward a spend threshold or cap used this year).
Personal verdicts: 'You paid Uber One with this card: credit applies' vs 'You don't subscribe: ignore this $120'.
Fee-vs-value per card from the user's actual use (credits recovered + rewards earned - fee).
Welcome-email intake: read card welcome emails/screenshots like the reference as evidence of which product/variant the user holds.
